summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly integrated AI/ML capabilities, driven by the production adoption of retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), with vector databases becoming critical infrastructure—75% of enterprise AI applications are projected to depend on vector search by 2026, and adoption grew 377% year over year. Platforms now range from fully managed AI suites with built-in LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML, Databricks Mosaic AI) to databases offering native vector search (MongoDB Atlas, Databricks) versus those relying on extensions (PostgreSQL/Aurora via pgvector). A key architectural caveat is that vector databases are specialized indexes for semantic search and should not be treated as universal data stores.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless access to hosted LLMs for tasks like summarization, translation, sentiment analysis, and completion via SQL/Python functions. Cortex Search enables semantic/hybrid retrieval, and Cortex Analyst allows natural-language querying. Snowflake Postgres (newly announced) further unifies the popular database with Snowflake's analytics and AI on a single governed platform via Horizon Catalog.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search is supported through the VECTOR data type and vector similarity functions (VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY, etc.), plus Cortex Search as a managed semantic search service.
databases.llm_integration: Native hosted LLMs (including Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) accessible directly via Cortex functions; no external API wiring required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits; Cortex LLM functions are billed per token/credit based on model size, separate from compute warehouse costs.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI integration, BigQuery Graph, and vector/hybrid search
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create and run ML models (regression, classification, time series, and remote Vertex AI/Gemini models) directly with SQL. It supports generating embeddings and building RAG applications with vector, text, and hybrid search, plus BigQuery Graph for relationship analysis. It positions itself as an autonomous data and AI platform with built-in predictive analytics and inferencing.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX, enabling semantic and hybrid search within SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models through remote models; ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING functions call foundation models directly from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) pricing for queries; AI/LLM inference and embedding generation incur additional Vertex AI charges based on usage.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector extension for vector storage/search and pgai for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: PostgreSQL gains AI capabilities through extensions: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity search, enabling a hybrid query pattern (relational + vector) within a single system, while pgai brings embedding generation and LLM calls into SQL. This 'keep everything together' approach is attractive but has noted performance limitations at extreme scale.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to core PostgreSQL—vector search is provided by the third-party pgvector extension (and accelerators like pgvectorscale). Core PostgreSQL alone does not include vector search.
databases.llm_integration: Via pgai extension, which enables calling external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) from SQL; depends on extension installation and configured API access.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; costs depend on hosting/managed provider (e.g., Timescale, Neon, RDS) plus any external LLM API fees for embedding/inference.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning (in-database ML via SQL to SageMaker, Bedrock, and Comprehend)
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models directly from SQL queries by integrating with Amazon SageMaker, Amazon Bedrock, and Amazon Comprehend. This enables predictions, sentiment analysis, and generative AI calls inline with transactional data without building separate pipelines.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search in Aurora ML itself; Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible supports vectors only via the pgvector extension, so this capability is extension-based rather than native.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models via SQL functions (aws_ml / aws_bedrock), allowing LLM inference inline with queries.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Aurora instance/storage/I-O pricing; ML inference calls incur separate SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend charges based on usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML (SQL-based model training/inference with SageMaker and Bedrock)
databases.description: Redshift ML enables data analysts and engineers to create, train, and deploy ML models using familiar SQL commands, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports bringing your own models and generative AI via Amazon Bedrock for in-warehouse inference on analytical data.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector search index in Redshift; it is oriented toward predictive ML and LLM inference rather than semantic vector retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with Amazon Bedrock LLMs and SageMaker models via SQL (CREATE MODEL / inference functions), allowing generative AI calls directly from the warehouse.
databases.pricing_notes: Redshift compute/storage pricing applies; model training and inference incur separate SageMaker and Bedrock charges based on usage.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Databricks offers Mosaic AI for building, fine-tuning, and serving ML/GenAI models and AI agents, tightly integrated with the Lakehouse and Unity Catalog governance. Databricks Vector Search provides a managed vector index synced with Delta tables for RAG and semantic search applications.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in managed vector search (Databricks Vector Search) with automatic sync from source Delta tables; no third-party extension required.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs provide access to open and proprietary LLMs (Llama, DBRX, external models), plus AI functions (ai_query) callable from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search, Model Serving, and foundation model inference are billed separately based on compute/endpoint usage.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search (native vector indexing and semantic/hybrid search)
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search stores embeddings alongside operational document data and performs approximate nearest-neighbor search within the same database, supporting RAG and semantic search with hybrid (vector + full-text + metadata) filtering. This keeps vectors and application data together without a separate vector store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native built-in vector search via the $vectorSearch aggregation stage and dedicated vector indexes within Atlas; no external extension needed.
databases.llm_integration: No bundled hosted LLMs, but strong integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, Amazon Bedrock, and others for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Part of Atlas managed service pricing (cluster tier/compute/storage); Vector Search runs on Atlas Search nodes which may incur additional dedicated resource costs.
